To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angular distributions of ions scattered from the surfaces of ferromagnetic materials have an anisotropic character.

we have developed a new method for measuring the magnetic field of a magnetic film, based on ion scattering, and we have used this method to study the magnetic fields of stripe domains of a magnetic film.
the anisotrophy of interaction of ions of the magnetic field of a stripe domain structure manifests itself in the wider angular range in the more adequate model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of using slow ions for investigation of the magnetic structure of thin films.
the development of a new approach for studying the magnetic properties of magnetic films by the method of ion scattering from the surface.
the possibility to study the magnetic domain structure of a sample by means of the method of ion scattering from the surface of the sample.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic domain structures are responsible for the angular distribution of ions scattered at low energies.
the angular distributions of the scattered ions are determined by the presence of the magnetic field of a stripe domain structure.
the magnetic field of stripe domain structure is responsible for the anisotropies in the angular distributions of ions scattered at the surface of magnetic film.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, within the model of diffuse scattering of ions, it is possible to reveal the presence of a domain structure of a magnetic film by the analysis of the angular distribution of scattered ions.

, within the framework of the model of diffuse scattering upon interaction of ions at the sample surface, the anisotropic distribution of slow ions scattered at small angles can be used for the determination of the parameters of the domain structure.

, for the magnetic films with a domain structure, the use of the diffuse scattering model is more adequate for the description of the angular distributions of scattered ions than the use of the specular scattering model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffuse scattering model allows for a better description of the experimental results.
the angular distributions of the scattered ions are strongly dependent on the model of scattering and on the parameters of the surface structure.
, in the case of diffuse scattering, a more adequate description of the interaction of ions with magnetic fields of surface magnetic domains is achieved.
